requirements.requirement: node3 (behind node1/lan-a) can reach node4's HTTP service on tcp/8080 (behind node2/lan-b) across the transit network
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.10.20.10:8080/ returns 'node4-http-ok' both before any restarts (cmd-fcdacf2612bb4c12), after node1's reboot (cmd-0b7e295ec27f490b), after node2's reboot (cmd-86843a55ccf24cc9), and after the final node4 service fix (cmd-da870763e73e4eac). Directly observed end-to-end success across both routers.

requirements.requirement: All other cross-network traffic between lan-a and lan-b remains refused by default
requirements.summary: ping, tcp/9999, and tcp/22 from node3 to node4 all fail/timeout (cmd-603e3f95756b4d7a, repeated post-fix in cmd-da870763e73e4eac). VyOS forward-filter counters directly show hits accruing on the default-drop rule (8 packets/528 bytes) while only the explicit 8080 rule matches allowed traffic (cmd-514a1cc354114490). Behavior reconfirmed after node1/node2 reboots (cmd-86843a55ccf24cc9).

requirements.requirement: VyOS (node1) forward filter is default-deny with a narrowly scoped explicit allow for the required flow
requirements.summary: op show firewall confirms default-action drop, rule 5 accepts established/related, rule 10 accepts only tcp/8080 from lan-a (10.10.10.0/24) to node4 (10.10.20.10/32) via eth2->eth1 (cmd-1d74cc758f6c4a54). Identical ruleset and route table persisted after the mandatory reboot (cmd-8a3054ee6d694c78).

requirements.requirement: OPNsense (node2) pf ruleset is default-deny with a narrowly scoped explicit allow, and existing SSH access on the mgmt interface is preserved
requirements.summary: pfctl -s rules shows the platform default catch-all block ('block drop in log inet all'), a single added pass rule restricted to vtnet1(opt1)/tcp/10.10.10.0/24->10.10.20.10 port http-alt(8080) (cmd-f53050f15c684580, cmd-7a8a72d54a764a37), and the pre-existing vtnet0 SSH pass rule left intact. The identical rule and route state is confirmed present after node2's reboot (cmd-adf8c0e9219141c6). Note: one executor-cited evidence ID for this requirement (cmd-7a1a8d8b53994a79) does not exist in the trace (likely a transcription typo for cmd-7a1a8d8b53094a79, which itself pertains to node4, not node2's ruleset) — a minor report-accuracy issue, but the underlying rule state is independently confirmed by the valid IDs cited here.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id e98d9010... captured healthy (cmd-dc01c118655c4681), reboot triggered (cmd-e9934552e5144e24), connection loss then recovery observed (cmd-7a179d523be84f33 through cmd-6c806d1b32a043aa) with new boot_id bdbce64f..., and interfaces/route/firewall config fully restored post-reboot (cmd-8a3054ee6d694c78). Cross-checked by global boot-identity snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime sec 1788676206 captured (cmd-b1e3fe9c7a444482), reboot triggered (cmd-f935c7d2748142bd), timeouts during reboot (cmd-f3ad9d3412294595) then recovery with new boottime sec 1788676918 (cmd-6d4d0ef0b08e467a), and interfaces/route/pf ruleset fully restored post-reboot (cmd-adf8c0e9219141c6).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node3 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2ba78175... captured (cmd-42abe7f97ec04122), reboot triggered (cmd-d987db20925f4641), connection refused then recovery (cmd-523a54ce04374925, cmd-71cebd3d62fd47d4) with new boot_id 7ef124ae..., and static IP/route via systemd-networkd plus working HTTP path confirmed restored post-reboot (cmd-cb835be5c3b54206).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node4 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state (including HTTP service persistence)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id f6f9440e... and reboot (cmd-609918935e094885) with new boot_id 89ab8496-e16d... confirmed (cmd-9d1483612bd7459e). The reboot directly exposed a real failure: the /tmp-based demo-http.service did not survive reboot (CHDIR error, cmd-32260a0fefa6437c, cmd-d8af739f999b470e), which the executor diagnosed and fixed by moving content to /srv/www and restarting the unit (cmd-7a1a8d8b53094a79), with connectivity re-confirmed from node3 (cmd-da870763e73e4eac). This is a legitimate and well-evidenced recovery, but the corrected persistent configuration was never itself verified by triggering a further reboot, so persistence of the fix specifically is not directly demonstrated.

overall_summary: The core task contract is satisfied with direct, repeated evidence: node3 reaches node4's HTTP service on tcp/8080 through both routers, all other cross-network traffic (ping, other TCP ports) is refused, and both VyOS and OPNsense show default-deny forward/pf rulesets with a single narrowly scoped explicit allow, verified both before and after mandatory reboots. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with clear boot-identity transitions and recovered configuration state; node4's restart genuinely exposed a real persistence bug (non-persistent /tmp-based HTTP service) which was diagnosed and corrected, though the fix itself was not re-validated across a second reboot. Minor residue (an unremoved OPNsense config backup file) and a mismatched evidence-ID citation in the executor's report slightly reduce confidence but do not affect the demonstrated functional outcome.
limitations: One executor-cited evidence ID for the OPNsense requirement (cmd-7a1a8d8b53994a79) does not exist in the captured trace; the closest match (cmd-7a1a8d8b53094a79) actually pertains to the node4 HTTP-service fix, not node2's ruleset — the OPNsense requirement was independently verified using other valid command IDs.

The node4 HTTP service persistence fix (moving from /tmp/www to /srv/www) was verified only via local and cross-node curl, not by triggering an additional reboot, so full persistence of that specific fix across a future restart is not directly observed.
An OPNsense config.xml backup file created during editing (/conf/config.xml.bak.<timestamp>) was not shown to be cleaned up in the trace.
Executor evidence item 4 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-7a1a8d8b53994a79

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to legitimate purposes: temporary IP assignments used to discover the correct transit/lan interface mapping via ARP (cmd-ba9771c391f84b58, cmd-6dc3997640ac41c4, cmd-9fc1b1baeb9e4cf6, cmd-da36cf4cf1594fe9, cmd-cf6b2ed64bfa4597, cmd-a24d4ff8de4b429b, cmd-2581c363980d4670, cmd-4fe2f15d85d74549, cmd-1fb1151202c14f79, cmd-cf92ed2e76074b0d, cmd-72826a6767fa4659, cmd-96850f3214e84d63, cmd-b62009d3d51844b3, cmd-6ca39ffe77b940b7, cmd-a62a22a8f1d1493b) were all bounded discovery/troubleshooting and were fully flushed/reverted before final configuration (cmd-922b6af34a154b4d, cmd-bc42d2ed86a74949, cmd-46cfb48bbc834d01, cmd-972b8ad720af486f). Temporary helper scripts (/tmp/f1.py-f4.py) used to edit OPNsense config.xml were removed (cmd-6f71ffeedcfb4354). A backgrounded tcpdump diagnostic that hit a proxy timeout was killed promptly (cmd-160ad69c90ba4fb0), a read-only diagnostic with no lasting effect. One residual artifact was left behind: the OPNsense config backup file created by cmd-143aa4ad74594185 (/conf/config.xml.bak.<timestamp>) was never removed — a low-risk, non-destructive retained file. The node4 demo-http.service's initial /tmp-based design (cmd-f89afd5fd6d2456e) was a reasonable first implementation that failed only because /tmp is wiped on reboot; this was directly diagnosed and corrected (cmd-7a1a8d8b53094a79) rather than being an unnecessary mutation. Reboot log files (/tmp/reboot.log) were cleaned up on all nodes at the end (cmd-e5ba2b0c20254132, cmd-ec4cfe11052c4e21, cmd-d01071b315dd4923, cmd-8846152899924da7).
